title: Profiteroles with salted caramel
subtitle: choux pastry puffs filled with whipped cream and finished with a salted caramel sauce
excerpt: Profiteroles with salted caramel are small choux pastry balls filled with lightly whipped cream and poured with a warm salted caramel sauce at the table. The choux shells are hollow and crisp, the cream cool and yielding inside, and the caramel gives a buttery, bitter-sweet top. They are assembled just before serving so the pastry stays crisp.
sourceNotes: Profiteroles are a classic French patisserie, the small choux ball a close relative of the eclair. The traditional accompaniment is hot chocolate sauce. Salted caramel became the more fashionable British alternative from the 2000s onward, particularly following the influence of Pierre Herme and Christophe Michalak.

glossaryTerms.definition: A cooked pastry dough made by heating water, butter, and flour together then beating in eggs. It puffs into a hollow shell during baking due to the steam trapped inside.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze unfilled choux balls once cooled. Defrost at room temperature and refresh in a 160 degrees C oven for 5 minutes before filling.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Bake the shells up to 8 hours ahead and store in an airtight container. Make the caramel sauce up to 2 days ahead. Fill and assemble just before serving.

content.text: Profiteroles with salted caramel are small

balls, baked hollow, then split and filled with softly whipped cream before the salted caramel sauce goes over at the table. The key to crisp profiteroles is drying them fully in the oven and piercing them immediately after baking so steam can escape. Fill them no more than 20 minutes before serving.

Make the choux: bring the water and butter to a rolling boil. Remove from the heat, add the sifted flour all at once and beat until smooth. Return to the heat and cook, stirring, for 1 minute until the paste leaves the sides of the pan. Cool for 5 minutes, then beat in the eggs gradually until the paste is smooth, glossy, and drops slowly from the spoon.

Heat the oven to 200 degrees C (fan 180 degrees C / gas 6). Line baking trays with baking paper. Pipe or spoon walnut-sized rounds of choux paste onto the trays, spaced 5 cm apart. Bake for 22 to 25 minutes until deep golden and hollow-sounding when tapped. Pierce the base of each with a skewer straight from the oven. Cool on a rack.

Make the salted caramel sauce: heat the caster sugar in a medium saucepan over medium heat without stirring until it caramelises to a deep amber. Carefully pour in the warmed cream in a steady stream (it will bubble hard). Stir until smooth. Add the butter and salt and stir until the butter is melted. Keep warm or reheat gently before serving.

Whip the double cream with the icing sugar to soft, billowy peaks. Transfer to a piping bag. Split each profiterole across the top or pipe cream in through the base hole. Place on a serving plate and pour the warm salted caramel sauce over the top at the table.

attrs.problem: Profiteroles soft and soggy rather than crisp
attrs.avoid: Avoid underbaking or filling them too early; both cause the shells to go soft.
attrs.fix: Bake until deeply golden. Pierce each one immediately from the oven. Fill no more than 20 minutes before serving and keep in a cool room, not the fridge.

attrs.problem: Caramel sauce seizing when the cream is added
attrs.avoid: Avoid cold cream; the temperature difference shocks the caramel and causes it to harden.
attrs.fix: Warm the cream to just below the boil before adding. Pour it into the caramel slowly and stir without stopping.
